label: early steps (t=2-4) after an x among the first two tokens
explanation: Fires during the early original phase (steps 2-4, ~97% of mass at t=2..4) of sequences whose first token is x (68% of mass, 16x lift) or whose second token is x (then only from t=3). It starts two steps after the x and turns off by t=5, regardless of what token is currently input (in_tok is flat). Strongest in sequences beginning with repeated x (x x x ...), peaking at t=3-4. Weak, low-quartile tail at t=5 and at the delimiter for short x-initial sequences; also faint activations when x is at position 2. Does not fire at t=0-1, in the copy phase, or for sequences with no early x. Dev: P 0.875, R 0.821, F1 0.847, mass recall 0.95.

issues: Minor: the predicate uses phase<=1, so it includes the delimiter step when L=3 or 4. On test, those steps have precision 0.37 (5653 predicted, 1.1% of mass). Limiting the predicate to phase==0 gives test P 0.909, R 0.795, F1 0.848, a little better than the reported 0.845. The explanation calls the delimiter step part of the 'weak tail', which is consistent with this, but it is a small mismatch between predicate and explanation.

The 'x at position 2' tail is real but weak, as the explanation says. With orig(2)==x, no x in the first two positions, and t==4, precision is 0.37, it covers 6.5% of active steps, and it holds 2.0% of mass. Adding it to the predicate lowers test F1 to 0.838, so leaving it out is reasonable. x at position 3 does not fire (precision 0.003).

The claims hold up. t=0-1 has 0 active steps. The copy phase has 20 of 2.73M steps (precision 7e-6). Steps 2-4 hold 97.4% of mass and t=5 holds 2.5%. Sequences whose first token is x hold 68% of mass at 16x lift. With orig(1)=x and orig(0)!=x, t=3 has precision 0.89, and t=2 does not fire. Steps with orig(0)=orig(1)=x have precision 1.0 and about 2.5x the mass per step. Rates by in_tok are flat (1.1-1.2x).

Remaining misses are mostly low-activation: the bottom quartile is only 40% covered, and misses hold 5% of mass in total. They come from t=5 after an early x, x at position 2, and short delimiter steps, all of which the explanation describes. False positives are spread out: at t=4 with orig(0)=x precision is 0.73-0.91 depending on the token class of orig(1), which is not a systematic pattern.
